summary:
Outpost is a 3D strategy game built in Unity that trains young explorers to think like astronauts on Mars. Players run a small Martian base for a 10-sol mission. Each sol they get only 3 actions to keep three vital resources in balance: Energy, Oxygen and Protection.

Outpost answers the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by turning real mission constraints (limited resources, planning and risk management) into simple, replayable gameplay.
details:
Outpost

Outpost is a 3D strategy game built in Unity that puts young players in charge of a small base on Mars. Their goal is to keep the base alive for 10 sols (Martian days), while dealing with the surprises of life on the Red Planet: dust storms and solar radiation.


The mission briefing welcomes the player to Outpost.

How does it work?

The base depends on three vital resources, shown at the top left of the screen:

  • Energy : produced by the solar panels.
  • Oxygen : needed for the base to stay alive. Making it costs energy.
  • Protection : the shield that keeps the base safe from radiation. It costs both oxygen and energy.


A short tutorial explains the rules in a few lines so kids can start playing right away.

Each day, the player has only 3 actions. They click the bubbles above the buildings to choose what to do. Before confirming, every action shows its cost and what it gives back.

For example reinforcing the shield costs 1 action 15 oxygen and 20 energy and gives +1 protection against radiation.

Then the player moves on to the next day. During the night the base uses up oxygen and energy just as a real habitat does. The player has to plan ahead. Spending everything today can leave the base without enough oxygen tomorrow.

Mars fights back: weather and forecasts

The rover announces tomorrow’s weather so the player can prepare:

  • Calm days : with normal conditions.
  • Dust storms : which block sunlight and cut solar energy production in half.
  • Solar flares : which cause radiation spikes. Without enough protection, the base is in danger and can be destroyed if the base as no protection.


A dust storm reduces the energy produced by the solar panels.


Radiation particles hit the base during a solar flare.

If the player keeps the base running until sol 10, the mission is accomplished.

Benefits and intended impact

Outpost turns abstract space science into concrete choices. Kids don’t just read that Mars has radiation and dust storms; they feel the consequences of their decisions. They learn the core skills of an astronaut: planning ahead, anticipating risks, managing limited resources and understanding that every choice has a cost. Each game is short and replayable, so it works well in classrooms or at home.

Tools and technologies

  • Unity 6 for the 3D engine.
  • C# for all gameplay systems : actions and costs, resource consumption, weather forecasts and events, and the user interface.
  • NASA open data (Curiosity RAD radiation measurements) used as a reference to set realistic game values.
  • Canva for the presentation.
  • Developed and tested on a Windows PC and MacOS.

Creativity

Instead of a quiz or a slideshow, Outpost teaches through gameplay. The science is built into the rules themselves. A solar flare is not just a fact on a screen; the rover warns you it is coming, and you must decide whether to spend your oxygen and energy on the shield or take the risk. The colorful, stylized 3D base makes the experience friendly and accessible for young players.

Factors our team considered

  • Age-appropriate design: 3 actions, 3 resources, clear gauges, a short tutorial, and costs shown before every action.
  • Learning through consequences: resources are used up every night, so kids learn to plan ahead.
  • Scientific accuracy: values based on real data, while keeping the game fun and readable.
  • Short sessions: a full mission takes a few minutes, which fits classroom use.
  • Scientific accuracy: values inspired by real NASA data, simplified so the game stays fun and easy to read for kids.
